items.t: angels brought near. And he said: Embark in it; in the name of God is its sailing /fol. 179r./ and its anchoring. Truly my Lord is Forgiving, Compassionate (Q 11:41) — then Ibn ʿAbbās turned to his companions and said: If it sinks, his debt is upon me.
Chapter 18 (al-bāb al-thāmin ʿashar): On the occult properties of the Throne Verse (Q 2:255) and the God-given (ladunnī) blessings that belong to it [284]

Know — may God grant success to me and to you in obedience to Him and in the understanding of His secrets — that the names have significative meanings, and that among the greatest and most majestic of the names is that which some of the eminent righteous ones, from among the masters of [spiritual] states, of inner discernment (iṭṭilāʿ), and of the names, have pointed out: that the greatest verse in the Book of God is the magnified, honoured Throne Verse, on account of His words, exalted is He, His Footstool embraces the heavens and the earth (Q 2:255); and that in His words, exalted is He, Alif-Lām-Mīm (Q 2:1) there is a majestic meaning, for the alif is from Allāh, and the lām from To Him belongs whatever is in the heavens and the earth (Q 2:255), and the mīm from Master of all Dominion (Q 3:26). And know that when this noble verse was sent down upon the Prophet — God bless him and grant him peace — forty thousand angels descended with it, in reverence and in magnification of its worth. So know the worth of what has come to you, for it is the delivering verse and the preventing verse, the repelling verse and the protecting verse; and it is the mistress of the Qurʾān, and it is a third of the Qurʾān. That has come down in sound hadiths. And it has come down that whoever recites it at the beginning of the night, no devil comes near him; and likewise whoever recites it at the beginning of the day, and there comes to him the Obeyed Master (al-sayyid al-muṭāʿ) for the understanding of the unveiling of the Throne Verse. And the Throne Verse is reckoned at one hundred and seventy letters, fifty words, and seven sections. And whoever recites it according to the number of its letters — one hundred and seventy times — and desires intercession with one possessed of authority, whoever he may be, his intercession is accepted. And whoever recites it while he is in hardship — the aforementioned number, one hundred and seventy times — in the depth of the night, in a state of ablution and facing the qibla, God, exalted is He, grants him relief soon. And whoever recites it the number of its words over some small quantity [of a thing], blessing is put into it, and it is guarded from the promptings of Satan. And whoever recites it the number of its sections on a Friday, after the afternoon prayer, in a place free of voices, in a state of ablution and facing the qibla, will find within [himself], and his heart will be in a state such as he has never known before, and in humility; so let him supplicate God, exalted is He, and he will be answered with the good of this world and of the hereafter. And whoever recites it in the middle of the night two hundred and twenty-five times is made secure from his enemy, and God, exalted is He, destroys him and takes him away from him. And whoever recites it three hundred and thirteen times to seek provision and to draw it in, it comes to him, and love for him goes forth to the whole of creation. And whoever is troubled by some matter and recites it three hundred and thirteen times, God suffices him against what troubles him in the affair of his religion and of his world, and opens for him the door of good things for as long as he keeps reciting it.

Let him recite this noble verse and write it in separated letters in a glass bowl with saffron, rose-water, and musk, and let it be drunk according to the number of its letters, over [that many] days; and let him be fasting, /fol. 179v./ and let him break his fast with nothing but it: God, exalted is He, will make him speak with the varieties of wisdom. And let the beginning of the operation be in the month of Nīsān; and if he adds to it some of its water, that is better. And when he wishes to break the fast upon the verse as we have mentioned, let him recite the Throne Verse seven times and say: "O God, I ask You by the right of this noble verse that You inspire me with Your God-given (ladunnī) knowledge. I ask You for a knowledge from among the sciences" — and let him name it; for God, exalted is He, grants success to your request. And I counselled one of the brethren to that, and he put it to use, and he had not completed the aforementioned number before God opened to him with diverse sciences, and he attained what he had been seeking, and beyond what could be added. And God guides whom He wills to a straight path (Q 2:213). And among its occult properties: when you put on a new garment, you recite it at the sewing of the garment and at the putting on of it, saying: "O God, as You have clothed me anew, [grant] that You make me live in felicity and appoint for me a lifespan increased." For the angels who are the servant-spirits (khuddām) of this verse ask forgiveness for the wearer of that garment until it wears out. And if he adds to it the sura Truly We sent it down on the Night of Power (Q 97:1), that is better.

And among the occult properties of this noble verse: when you visit a sick man, ask him about the condition of his illness. If his illness is from a headache in his head, or a pain, you write it out for him in separated letters and hang it upon him on the side of the pain and the ache. And if the sick man tells you that his ache is from his interior, or from his whole body, then draw its renowned wafq in a glass bowl, the writing being with musk, saffron, and rose-water; then write the noble verse also in separated letters, and write with it the verses of healing, which are His words, exalted is He: and He will heal the breasts of a believing people (Q 9:14); and a healing for what is in the breasts, and a guidance and a mercy for the believers (Q 10:57); in it is a healing for mankind (Q 16:69); And We send down of the Qurʾān that which is a healing and a mercy for the believers (Q 17:82); And when I fall sick, it is He who heals me (Q 26:80); Say: for those who believe it is a guidance and a healing (Q 41:44). Then the writing is effaced with bees' honey, and the noble verse is recited over it seven times, and the sick man drinks it: he will be restored to health by the leave of God, exalted is He.

And among the occult properties of this generous verse: whoever is afflicted by phlegm — let him take seven pieces of small white salt and recite over each one of them the noble verse seven times, and let him use them on an empty stomach for seven successive days, for God takes away from him what he suffers. And it is related of one of them that he used to see in his sleep frightening matters and things that terrified him, so he came to one of the masters, of /fol. 180r./ those possessed of operative deployment (taṣrīf), and complained to him of what he was finding in his sleep. The master said to him: When you betake yourself to your bed, seek refuge in God from the accursed Satan three times; then recite the Throne Verse three times, and when you reach His words, exalted is He, The guarding of them does not weary Him, and He is the Exalted, the Magnificent (Q 2:255), repeat it three times and go to sleep, and you will be safe from what you find. So the man did that, and after it he found nothing that he disliked.

And among the occult properties of the noble Throne Verse: when you wish to go in upon a king or a tyrant and you fear his mischief, you say, as you go in upon him, "Shāhat al-wujūh" ("may the faces be disfigured") three times; you recite the Throne Verse three times; then you say: "O God, cast [upon me] of Your adornment, and Your love, and Your honour, and the attributes of Your lordship, that whereby hearts are dazzled, and souls are abased, and eyes flash, and thoughts are made dull, and every arrogant tyrant is made to submit. O al-ʿAzīz (the Mighty), O al-Ghaffār (the All-Forgiving), O Allāh, O al-Wāḥid (the One), O al-Aḥad (the Unique). O God, guard me in what You have given me to possess, by that whereby You are more its possessor than I am; and supply me with a subtle strand from the subtle strands of Your name al-Ḥafīẓ (the Preserver), and snatch away thereby the sights of all existing things; and clothe me in a coat of mail of Your sufficing and Your safekeeping; and gird me with the sword of Your aid, and Your honour, and Your protection; and crown me with the crown of Your might and Your honour; and wrap me in the mantle of Your favour and Your well-being; and mount me upon the vessel of deliverance unto death; and supply me with a subtle strand from the subtle strands of Your names of subduing, and repel from me thereby whoever intends evil against me from among the whole of Your creation, as You made the sea subservient to Moses son of ʿImrān; and soften their hearts for me as You softened iron for David — peace be upon him — for they do not speak save by Your leave; their forelocks are in Your grasp, which You turn about as You will. O Turner of hearts, O Knower of all unseen things: I have quenched the wrath of So-and-so son of So-and-so" — and if you wish, you may say, "I have quenched the wrath of the people" — "by 'there is no god but God'; and I have drawn their hearts by Muḥammad, the Messenger of God, God bless him and grant him peace.

And when they saw him they magnified him, and they cut their hands, and they said: God forbid! This is no mortal; this is nothing but a noble angel (Q 12:31). And there is no power and no strength save in God, the Exalted, the Mighty. And a guarding against every rebellious devil (Q 37:7); and a guarding — that is the ordaining of the Mighty, the All-Knowing (Q 41:12); and We have guarded it from every accursed devil (Q 15:17); Truly it is We who have sent down the Reminder, and truly We are its guardians (Q 15:9); He has attendant angels before him and behind him, guarding him by the command of God (Q 13:11); and God encompasses them round about; nay, it is a glorious Qurʾān, upon a preserved Tablet (Q 85:20–22); and truly we are his guardians (Q 12:12); and We delivered him from the distress, and thus do We deliver the believers (Q 21:88); and I am not a guardian over you (Q 6:104); there is no soul but has a guardian over it (Q 86:4); But if they turn away, say: God suffices me; there is no god but He. Upon Him I rely, and He is the Lord /fol. 180v./ of the Mighty Throne (Q 9:129); God is Guardian over them, and you are not a trustee over them (Q 42:6)." He says: "Ḥafīẓ, Ḥafīẓ, Ḥafīẓ. O al-Ḥāfiẓ (the Guardian), O al-Ḥafīẓ (the Preserver), guard us! O God, watch over us with Your eye that does not sleep, and shelter us within Your shelter that cannot be assailed. O Allāh, O Allāh, O Lord of the worlds." Then you fall silent, you and whoever is with you, and you do not speak; for even if the whole nation of Rabīʿa and Muḍar were to come in upon you, they would not harm you nor injure you, and God would hide you from them. And I have tried it many times over. So understand that, and you will be rightly guided.

And know, my brother — may God, exalted is He, grant success to us and to you in the understanding of His secrets — that this noble verse and these lofty names were sent down from beneath the leg of the Throne; and when it was sent down upon the Messenger of God — God bless him and grant him peace — seventy thousand angels descended with it, in honour and in magnification of it. And it is the deliverer from fear and terror, and from the evil of humankind and of jinn. And whoever recites it in places of fear is made secure and guarded and sufficed, for it is the verse of guarding. And it has seventy-two operative deployments (taṣrīf); but I have turned away from mentioning them for fear of the ignorant, lest it fall into the hand of one who does not know its worth, so that he violates by it what is sacrosanct and does with it what does not befit it. And we have [nonetheless] opened the door for whoever wishes to enter into this treasure, mighty in station. And God guides whom He wills to a straight path (Q 2:213).

And among the occult properties of the Throne Verse: when a person sets out on a journey and is about to leave his house, let him say: "A thousand, a thousand, a thousand Qul huwa Llāhu aḥad (Sūrat al-Ikhlāṣ) and the Throne Verse — by them I fortify property and family and child. A thousand, a thousand Qul huwa Llāhu aḥad and the

Throne Verse are at my right and at my left — by them I guard myself against every one. I have put on the veil of God, the All-Encompassing, the Exalted; and I have fortified myself in the fortress of God, the Pre-eternal; and I have girded myself with the sword of the Commander of the Faithful ʿAlī; and I have wrapped myself in the mantle of ʿĀʾisha, Mother of the Believers; and I have entered into the treasuries of 'In the name of God, the All-Merciful, the Compassionate', whose locks are 'Praise be to God, Lord of the worlds'." Then he recites the Throne Verse and Qul huwa Llāhu aḥad three times, and blows to his right and to his left. And if he wishes to abridge it, let him recite what we have mentioned, then blow into his palms and wipe with them his head and his face and the rest of his body; for God, exalted is He, makes him secure from all that he fears and is wary of, until he returns to his dwelling.

And among its occult properties: whoever recites it in the morning, God, exalted is He, keeps him secure until he comes to the evening; or in the evening, God keeps him secure until he comes to the morning. And among its occult properties: if you recite it over the head of an epileptic (maṣrūʿ) eleven times, he comes to his senses on the spot; and if the afflicting [spirit] (al-ʿāriḍ) persists and does not come out of the body, it is burnt. And among its occult properties: if it is recited immediately after the prayers, it effaces the faults and the slips that lie upon the one who prays. And among its occult properties: if it is recited when going in /fol. 181r./ upon a tyrant or an unjust ruler — and one says in the course of it: "O God, O Living, O Self-Subsisting, O Wondrous Originator of the heavens and the earth, O Dhū l-Jalāl wa-l-Ikrām (Possessor of Majesty and Honour), I ask You by the right of this generous verse and by what is in it of the secrets of understanding, that You bridle his mouth against me and strike his tongue dumb against me, so that he speak nothing but good, or else keep silent. Your good, O you, is before you, and your evil is beneath your feet" — and he goes in upon him: God bridles his mouth, and there accrues to him other than harm, if God, exalted is He, wills.

And among its occult properties: if you fear the evil of someone and harm has come to you from him, then you pray two rakʿas after the evening prayer, with the Fātiḥa and the Throne Verse. And when it is the last prostration, the Throne Verse is recited three times while you are prostrate; and when you reach His words, exalted is He, The guarding of them does not weary Him, and He is the Exalted, the Magnificent (Q 2:255), you repeat it three times, or seven. You say in the course of your recitation: "O God, come between me and So-and-so son of So-and-so, as You have come between the heaven and the earth; and bridle his mouth against me, as You bridled the beasts of prey away from Daniel — peace be upon him — by the right of these noble names." For you will be secure from his evil, and you will bridle his mouth against you, so that he will not speak of you save with good.

And among its occult properties: if you are in a company of people and you desire to be sufficed against their evil and their harm, recite the generous verse three times and blow into your palms three times, and wipe with your hand over your face and your whole body, while you say:

"O God, suffice me against the evil of these people, O Sufficer; and grant me well-being from their harm, O Granter of well-being." For God will make you secure from them, and no evil from them will befall you, by the leave of God, exalted is He. And among the occult properties of this magnificent verse: if you recite it by night, you are secure until the morning; and if you recite it by day, you are secure until the evening.

And it is related that a man lodged in an abandoned house; and when night fell upon him, lo, there was a foulness and a clangour. The man looked, and there was a black figure, with fire issuing from his nostrils, crawling upon the ground and making toward him. He said: When I saw him I feared him with a great fear, and I was inspired to recite the Throne Verse; and every time I said a word, he said it with me — until I reached His words, exalted is He, The guarding of them does not weary Him, and He is the Exalted, the Magnificent (Q 2:255), and he did not say it. So I repeated it upon him many times over, and he vanished from me, and I did not see him for the remainder of my night. And when it was morning I looked, and lo, one of the corners of the house was ashes; and I marvelled at that. Then I told my story to a brother of mine among my brethren, and he was a righteous man, and he said to me: This was an ʿifrīt who wished to harm you, and this generous verse burnt him, because you were inspired to recite it. And when I heard that, I took it as a litany (wird) and a remembrance by night and by day; and I saw of its blessing something mighty. /fol. 181v./

And among its occult properties: it is written for the companion-spirits (quranāʾ) and the attendant spirits (tawābiʿ); for whoever has it hung upon him is made secure from that. And if there be joined to it His words, exalted is He, and God encompasses them from behind; nay, it is a majestic Qurʾān, upon a preserved Tablet (Q 85:20–22); God is the best guardian, and He is the Most Merciful of the merciful (Q 12:64); He has attendant angels before him and behind him, guarding him by the command of God (Q 13:11); But if they turn away, say: God suffices me; there is no god but He. Upon Him I rely, and He is the Lord of the Mighty Throne (Q 9:129); and a guarding against every rebellious devil (Q 37:7); and We have guarded it from every accursed devil (Q 15:17); and a guarding — that is the ordaining of the Mighty, the All-Knowing (Q 41:12) — and there is written with it al-Ikhlāṣand the two suras of refuge-seeking (al-Muʿawwidhatān), then it is a mighty veil against the companion-spirits and others, if God, exalted is He, wills.

And among the occult properties of this verse: when it is placed among goods, they are preserved, and their owner is made secure over them against thieves and others. And when the generous verse is drawn in the wafq of the Sun — be it numerical or literal — in the hour of the Sun, and then placed among the loads of merchandise, they increase and yield profit. And if the aforementioned square is placed in the money chest, it is preserved, and the money is not emptied out of the chest so long as the noble square is in it. And among the occult properties of this verse, which is His words, exalted is He, Alif-Lām-Mīm. God — there is no god but He, the Living, the Self-Subsisting (Q 3:1–2): this noble verse contains the Greatest Name of God, and it has, of number, 483. Whoever sets it down by the secret of interpenetration (al-tadākhul) in the first [hour] of the day of Friday upon a noble body, and carries it with him, sees of the wonders of God's making, exalted is He, what descriptions fall short of, in the way of high standing, might, and awe in the eyes of people. And in it is a marvellous secret for going in upon rulers, kings, grandees and viziers, and for the seeking of needs. And this is the form of its arrangement, as you see:
