And it is related from al-Ḥasan b. ʿAlī — may God ennoble his face — that he said: I am surety for whoever recites this verse, up to twenty verses of it, that God, exalted is He, will preserve him from every rebellious devil, and from every wrongdoer, and from every treacherous thief, and from every ravening beast of prey — the Throne Verse, and three verses from al-Aʿrāf, Indeed your Lord is God (Q 7:54), and ten verses from the beginning of al-Ṣāffāt, and three verses from al-Raḥmān, O company of jinn and mankind, if you are able to pass beyond the confines of the heavens and the earth (Q 55:33), and the closing verses of Sūrat al-Ḥashr, and the end of Sūrat Tabbat. And among the occult properties of the noble Throne Verse: when some matter troubles one of you, let him perform the ablution in the depth of the night and pray two rakʿas, each rakʿa with the Fātiḥa and the Throne Verse three times; /fol. 182r./ and when he has given the salutation, you recite the noble verse seven times, and after it he says this blessed supplication: "O God, truly You hear my speech, and see my place, and know my secret and my open state, and nothing of my affair is hidden from You. I supplicate You with the supplication of the destitute, the poor, who cries for help, who seeks refuge, who confesses his sin and his shortcoming; and I ask You with the asking of the needy; and I entreat You with the entreaty of the lowly sinner — the entreaty of one whose neck is bowed before You, and whose tear has overflowed toward You, and who has abased his cheek before You and rubbed his nose in the dust for You: that You quicken our hearts, and expand our breasts, and make our endeavours pure for Your generous Face and a cause of attaining to bliss. And grant us success, our Lord, in that which is Your pure good pleasure; and seal for us from Yourself with good; and make us tomorrow with those upon whom You have bestowed favour — of the prophets, and the truthful, and the martyrs, and the righteous; and how excellent are those as companions! And suffice us, O God, in what troubles us of the affair of religion, and of this world, and of the hereafter; and do not let the enemies gloat over us, nor the envious folk; and do not make our affliction to be in our religion; and do not make this world our greatest care, nor the sum of our knowledge; and do not, because of our sins, give power over us to one who does not fear You and does not have mercy upon us; and let us enjoy our hearing and our sight; and give us life; and open for us the doors of good; and provide for us, for You are the best of providers (Q 5:114); Our Lord, forgive us, and our brethren who preceded us in faith, and put not in our hearts any rancour toward those who have believed (Q 59:10); and forgive us — our Lord, truly You are Ever-Gentle, Compassionate (Q 59:10); Our Lord, forgive us our sins and our excess in our affair, and make firm our feet, and give us victory over the unbelieving people (Q 3:147); Our Lord, give us good in this world and good in the hereafter, and guard us from the torment of the Fire (Q 2:201) — by Your mercy, O Most Merciful of the merciful."

And among the occult properties of this noble verse: if it is written upon the shroud of a dead man in three places — it is written at his head, and at his middle, and at his shins — then that dead man is not tormented in his grave, and the two angels deal gently with him at the time of the questioning; for it is the greatest verse in the Qurʾān, and He began it with His generous name, and He said — mighty and majestic is He who speaks — God — there is no god but He, the Living, the Self-Subsisting (Q 2:255). So know, O you, its worth, and supplicate with it in weighty affairs and at the fulfilling of needs. And it is related also of one of the righteous that he said: I was in a ship, and the black wind rose against them, so that scarcely would anyone be saved from it. So he drew the Throne Verse upon a sheet of paper (qirṭās) and hung it facing the blowing of the wind, and spread out his palms to God, exalted is He, in supplication; and he says in his supplication: "O God, I ask You by Your magnificent name, /fol. 182v./ God — there is no god but He, the Living, the Self-Subsisting (Q 2:255) — to the end of it — I ask You, O God, by its blessing, that You deliver us from what has come down upon us; and You are the Knower of all unseen things and the Dispeller of distresses. I ask You, O God, by the deliverance of Your most generous beloved, Muḥammad — God bless him and grant him peace." And he had not completed his supplication before God, exalted is He, gave them relief, and the fair wind came to them, and they journeyed on in security, in safety, and in soundness.

And among the occult properties of this noble verse: whoever desires that God, exalted is He, heal him of every disease in his body and of all the pains and the sicknesses — and there is written with it His words, exalted is He, Had We sent down this Qurʾān upon a mountain, you would have seen it humbled, split asunder out of the fear of God (Q 59:21) — to the end of the sura — and His words, exalted is He, And if there were a Qurʾān by which the mountains were set moving, or by which the earth were cleft asunder, or by which the dead were spoken to — nay, but to God belongs the whole affair (Q 13:31). And when he has finished writing it, the Throne Verse is recited over it seven times, and you suffumigate it with whatever there may be of sweet perfumes, and he drinks it over three days, morning and evening: God, exalted is He, heals him and grants him well-being from everything he dislikes. And if he also writes it and hangs it upon him, that is more effective and better. And God is the Healer, and the Sufficer, and the Granter of well-being.
And among the occult properties of this noble verse: it is written for ophthalmia and for pain of the eye; it is written and hung upon him. The Throne Verse is written three times, and His words

…exalted is He: God is the light of the heavens and the earth; the likeness of His light…— to His words, exalted is He — and God is Knower of all things (Q 24:35); and you write Say: He is God, One (Q 112:1). In the eye is ophthalmia, a redness within a whiteness. God the Eternal Refuge is my sufficiency. O my Succour in hardships, by

Your being too mighty [to have] a child! There was no doubt concerning God, and none is equal to Him, not one. I adjure you, O ophthalmia, O inflamed one that clings to the veins and to the skins; for I adjure you by Joseph son of Jacob and his rent shirt, and by the Torah of Moses and the Gospel of Jesus and the Psalms of David, and by the Mighty Qurʾān, and by Muḥammad — God bless him and grant him peace — the lamp of existence and Messenger of the Lord who is worshipped: depart, O ophthalmia, from the bearer of this writing of mine, by the truth of "there is no god but God, Muḥammad is the Messenger of God", and by a thousand thousand "there is no power and no strength save in God, the High, the Mighty". And God bless our master Muḥammad and his family and his companions, and grant peace.

Among the occult properties of this noble verse: it is written for the weeping of children and hung upon them. You write the noble Fātiḥa in separated letters, and likewise the Throne Verse — you write it in separated letters, three times. And you write And God prevails over His affair (Q 12:21); But if they turn away, say: God suffices me; there is no god but He. Upon Him I rely, and He is the Lord of the Mighty Throne (Q 9:129). Ṣar ṣar ṣar ṣar, ṣah ṣah ṣah ṣah! Be still, O newborn, and be silent, by the sanctity of the Lord who is worshipped. And voices are humbled before the All-Merciful, so that you hear nothing but a hushed whisper (Q 20:108). And faces are humbled before the Living, the Self-Subsisting; and he who bears wrongdoing has failed (Q 20:111). Faces that day /fol. 183r./ shall be bright, laughing, rejoicing at good tidings (Q 80:38–39). Do you then marvel at this discourse, and laugh and not weep, while you divert yourselves heedlessly?(Q 53:59–61) — and you are silent! Be silent, O newborn, by the truth of the King who is worshipped and the Loving Lord! Kāf-Hāʾ-Yāʾ-ʿAyn-Ṣād, Ḥā-Mīm-ʿAyn-Sīn-Qāf. And God encompasses them from behind. Nay, it is a majestic Qurʾān, upon a preserved Tablet (Q 85:20–22) — preserved, preserved! I place under the protection of God, exalted is He, whoever has this writing of mine hung upon him, from the evil of what He has created; and I have fortified him by God, the Living who does not die. And lift, O God, evil and harm from the bearer of this writing of mine. I have fortified him with "there is no god but God, Muḥammad is the Messenger of God", and by the truth of "In the name of God, the All-Merciful, the Compassionate": Say: I take refuge with the Lord of the daybreak, from the evil of what He has created, and from the evil of the night-darkness when it closes in, and from the evil of those who blow upon the knots, and from the evil of an envier when he envies (Q 113:1–5) — by a thousand thousand "there is no power and no strength save in God, the High, the Mighty".

Among the occult properties of this noble verse, for the binding of tongues: the noble verse is written on Indian paper in separated letters, and there is written with it these names — nūw, then fūw, then nūwā: so they do not speak. Every king is a possession owned by God; and every rich man is, with God, a destitute pauper; and every tyrant is, with God, abased, and he has no refuge from God. I seek help against you, O

So-and-so son of So-and-so [f.], by God the Magnificent. And voices are humbled before the All-Merciful, so that you hear nothing but a hushed whisper (Q 20:108). And a bar is placed between them and that which they crave (Q 34:54). This is a day on which they shall not speak, nor shall they be given leave to make excuses (Q 77:35–36). So God will suffice you against them, and He is the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing (Q 2:137). Kāf-Hāʾ-Yāʾ-ʿAyn-Ṣād, Ḥā-Mīm-ʿAyn-Sīn-Qāf, Qāf, Nūn. Dumb, dumb, dumb, dumb, dumb; blind, blind, blind, blind, blind, blind, blind. So they do not see. So they do not speak. So they do not talk. And We have set before them a barrier and behind them a barrier, and We have covered them over, so they do not see (Q 36:9). I have bound your tongue, O So-and-so son of So-and-so [f.], by that wherewith God bound the heavens from falling upon the earth save by His leave; and by that wherewith God bound the beasts of prey away from Daniel — peace be upon him; and by that wherewith God bound […] from giving birth; and by that wherewith God bound the barren wind, which leaves nothing that it comes upon but makes it like decayed bones (Q 51:42). And I have bound all the tongues of creation and of humankind, of every female and male among the children of Adam and the daughters of Eve, away from the bearer of this writing of mine: they shall not speak concerning him save with good, or else they shall be silent. Deaf, dumb, blind — so they do not speak. And God turned back those who disbelieved in their rage; they attained no good.
And God sufficed the believers in the fighting; and God is Strong, Mighty (Q 33:25).

[Among the occult properties of] the noble Throne Verse: if you have an enemy, or an obstinate adversary, or you fear the evil of a tyrannical ruler or an oppressive wrongdoer, and you wish to quench his evil away from you, or to destroy him if he deserves that — then, when it is the eve of Friday, rise at midnight, or in the last third [of the night], in a state of ablution, and pray two rakʿas with the intention of what you want of what we have mentioned. And you recite in the first the Fātiḥa once and the Throne Verse nine /fol. 183v./ times, and you do in the second rakʿa the like of the first; and when you have given the salām ⟨you recite the Throne Verse nine times and you do in the second rakʿa the like of the first; and when you have given the salām⟩he says the Throne Verse nine times also. Then you say: O God, You are severe in seizing-grip, painful in seizing, magnificent, Possessor of the subduing power that is exalted above opposites and peers, transcendent above consort and children. I ask You for the subduing of enemies and the crushing of tyrants. You devise against whom You will, and You are the best of devisers. I ask You by Your name before which forelocks are bowed low, by which You brought down [those who were] in the fortresses, and cast terror into the hearts of the enemies, and made wretched the people of wretchedness — I ask You to supply me with a subtle strand from among the subtle strands of this name, coursing through my enemies with the universal and the particular substances, until I am enabled to do what I will to him who has wronged me. I desire that no wrongdoer reach me with harm, and that no arrogant tyrant assault me; and make my anger for You and in You, conjoined with Your anger for Your own sake; and blot out the sight of my enemies, and harden their hearts, and strike between me and them a wall having a gate: its inner side, therein is mercy, and its outer side, facing it, is the torment. Truly You are severe in seizing-grip, painful in retribution. And such is the seizing of your Lord when He seizes the towns in their wrongdoing; truly His seizing is painful, severe (Q 11:102). And there is suited to it, of the verses of the Mighty Qurʾān: So God seized them for their sins, and they had no protector against God (Q 40:21); Truly the seizing-grip of your Lord is severe (Q 85:12); So He seized them with a mounting seizure (Q 69:10); So the last remnant of the people who did wrong was cut off; and praise be to God, the Lord of the worlds (Q 6:45). And you say: O God, I ask You, by the blessing and the secret of that wherewith I have called upon You, to subdue my enemies and whoever intends evil for me. And He is the Subduer above His servants (Q 6:18) — subdue So-and-so son of So-and-so [f.]! For I thrust You against his throat: so suffice me against his evil, and turn away from me his treachery and his guile, O Lord of the worlds. For God will preserve you and guard you from him, and you will be safe from his evil; and if he transgresses against you, he perishes forthwith. And if the invoker is the possessor of a truthful state, he does not rise from his place but that his need has succeeded. So understand. So whoever pardons and sets things right, his reward rests with God (Q 42:40); and God supports with His help whom He wills (Q 3:13). No servant has ever communed with God, exalted is He, by this litany of remembrance in the first [hour] of the day of Saturday and invoked against one who wronged him, but that he was seized on the spot.

Among the occult properties of the noble Throne Verse: if he has a need among pressing needs, then you enter one of the mosques and pray two rakʿas. You recite in the first rakʿa the Fātiḥa once and the Throne Verse seven times, and in the second rakʿa you do likewise. And when /fol. 184r./ you have given the salām, rise up by your own strength and stand in the prayer-niche (miḥrāb), and take hold of its sides with your hand and shake it; and say Yā Rabb (O Lord) seven times, and say Yā ʿAẓīm (O Magnificent) seven times, and say Yā Ḥalīm Yā Ḥalīm Yā Karīm Yā Raḥīm (O Forbearing, O Forbearing, O Generous, O Compassionate) seven times, and say Yā Qāḍī l-ḥājāt (O Fulfiller of needs) seven times. Then you say this blessed supplication: O Lord, enrich me by You, apart from all besides You, with a richness that makes me independent of every portion that summons to any outward creation or inward affair; and cause my innermost secret to reach [its term]; raise me to the Lote-tree of my own uttermost bound; and make me witness existence with vision and with joy, upon the secret of the sending-down to the endings and of munificence to the beginnings, until speech is cut off, and the movement of mankind grows still, and the dot of the ghayn is effaced, and the one stands in place of the two. O God, make easy for me [something] of the secret which You have made easy for many of Your servants; and support me in that with a resplendent light whereby the sight of every envier among jinn and humankind is snatched away; and grant me a lofty degree in every station; and enrich me, apart from all besides You, with a richness that establishes my poverty toward You. Truly You are the Self-Sufficient, the Praiseworthy. O God, I ask You to enrich my poverty, and to ease my affair, and to mend my brokenness, and to gather up my dishevelment and my abasement, and that You accomplish my need, which is such-and-such — and you ask for what you want: of the enriching of poverty, and the easing of an affair, and the removal of care and grief, and all that you want. For God, exalted is He, will grant you what you seek and what you want; and He is the most generous of those who are asked and the best of those who give. So make your opinion and your intention good, and you will attain your wish. And there is suited to it, of the verses of the Mighty Qurʾān, His words, exalted is He: Did He not find you an orphan and give shelter? And He found you erring and guided; and He found you in want and enriched (Q 93:6–8). So understand these strange indications. And God speaks the truth, and He guides to the way.
Among the occult properties of the noble Throne Verse: if you have a need with one of the great ones and you wish it to be fulfilled, then you fast that day from…

…greasy foods (al-zafar); and if you wish, your fasting that whole day would be better. And when the time of your breaking of the fast comes, break your fast upon something that is sweet. Then you pray the sunset prayer, and after the prayer you sit in your place of prayer and begin with the recitation of the Throne Verse; and you never speak any word of this world. And you continue thus until you pray the night prayer (ʿishāʾ). Then you sit [and recite] the Throne Verse seventeen times; and every time you have recited the verse once, you say in the course of your recitation: O God, make subservient to me the heart of So-and-so son of So-and-so [f.] — or So-and-so son of So-and-so. And you do not cease from that until you complete the number mentioned. And you say: O God, I ask You, O Living, O Abiding, O Everlasting, O Loving: I ask You to cast affection and love into the heart of So-and-so son of So-and-so [f.]; and to fulfil my need; and to seize hold of his heart with affection and love for me — and you name yourself — so that he be pliant to my hand and not oppose me in what I command him, by the right of Your name al-Wadūd (the Loving), and by the right of the secrets of this /fol. 184v./ noble verse. Take charge, O servant-spirits of the Throne Verse, of the drawing of the heart of So-and-so son of So-and-so [f.] to the heart of So-and-so son of So-and-so [f.]; and stir up the spiritual force of love and affection between me and him. They love them as God should be loved; but those who believe are stronger in love for God (Q 2:165). Had you spent all that is in the earth, you could not have joined their hearts in affection; but God joined them in affection. Truly He is Mighty, Wise (Q 8:63). And I cast upon you a love from Me, that you might be fashioned under My eye (Q 20:39).

Then you write upon clean paper (kāghad) what will be set out below, and the writing is to be with musk, saffron and rose-water. You write: In the name of God, the All-Merciful, the Compassionate. And you write: Ṭamūsh Ṭamūsh Yāṭūsh Yashṭūsh Yasṭūsh Saʿāb Saʿyāb Hīliyūthā Shaliyūthā Ahyāwush ʿAlshāqash Mahrāqash Shāʿūb Shīghūb Yaḥūm Saḥūm Marḥūm Daymūm Dayūm Ahyā Sharāhiyā Adūnāy Aṣbāʾūt Āl Shadāy. I have taken the meanings of the letters. And beneath them three verses, and the square of the felicities (wafq al-suʿūd), from the Sovereign who is worshipped and the good that is found. O servant-spirits of these names and these letters, stir up the spiritual force of love and affection between So-and-so son of So-and-so [f.] and So-and-so son of So-and-so [f.], by the right of what I have recited over you of the mighty names of God; and take hold of the gathering-points of his heart and his mind, so that he can utter nothing but my name, and look upon nothing but my person, and hear nothing but my word and my speech. Come forward, and do not fear; truly you are among those who are secure (Q 28:31). And I cast upon you a love from Me (Q 20:39). Wa-Daḥab Wa-Daḥab Wud Wud Wud. Love is obtained, drawn, drawn, like sugar in hearts. Draw, and attract, and endear, and make loving, and cast the robe of love, and the crown of awe, and the light of gnosis, by the majestic names and the mighty adjurations. Hayhayūh Ahyāhayūh! Abased is every tyrant before the awe of God's majesty, and submissive is every arrogant one to the command of God. Fear not, you two; truly I am with you both — I hear and I see (Q 20:46). You shall not fear being overtaken, nor shall you be afraid (Q 20:77). And when they saw him they magnified him, and they cut their hands, and they said: God forbid! This is no mortal; this is nothing but a noble angel (Q 12:31). Take charge, O servant-spirits of these names, of the fulfilment of the need of So-and-so from So-and-so. They do not disobey God in what He commands them, and they do what they are commanded (Q 66:6). Do, O So-and-so son of So-and-so [f.], what I have commanded you of the fulfilment of my need, and it is such-and-such — by the right of Him who said to the heavens and the earth: Come, willingly or unwillingly! They said: We come willingly (Q 41:11). Even so let So-and-so son of So-and-so [f.] obey So-and-so son of So-and-so [f.] in what he asks of him, and not oppose him in anything of the fulfilment of his needs. Take charge, O lord of this day and this hour — you and your helpers — and be all of you helpers to So-and-so son of So-and-so [f.] for the fulfilment of his need from So-and-so son of So-and-so [f.], by the right of these mighty verses and these generous adjurations, and by the right of God, the King, the All-Knowing. Hear and obey, O So-and-so son of So-and-so [f.], and fulfil the need of So-and-so son of So-and-so [f.]. Let no one speak concerning So-and-so son of So-and-so [f.] save with good, or /fol. 185r./ let him keep silent. This is a day on which they shall not speak, nor shall they be given leave to make excuses (Q 77:35–36). Make your excuse, O So-and-so son of So-and-so [f.], and fulfil for him all that he asks and all that he desires, by the right of God, the Praiseworthy, the Glorious, and by the right of Ṭahṭahūb Ṭahṭahūb

Lahūb Lahūb, the life of everything. No servant has disobeyed You but that he was burned, and no tyrant but that he was abased and perished. Hayd Hayd Wahā Hā Hū Hū Hū Ah Ah Yah Bīh Wah Wah. And He is the Subduer above His servants (Q 6:18). To Him belongs the lofty kingship and the towering might. You are He, He; and You are powerful over everything. I ask You, O God, that You make subservient to me Your generous angels who serve these names and who obey these adjurations, that they take charge and comply with what he has commanded them of assistance to So-and-so son of So-and-so [f.] against So-and-so son of So-and-so [f.]; and fulfil for him all that he asks, and make him pliant to his hand, not opposing him in any matter whatsoever. Come now! Haste! Speed! This very hour! May God bless you and pour blessing upon you.

And you write this noble wafq whose mention comes next. Then you suffumigate the paper with fine Indian aloeswood, benzoin (jāwī), mastic, pepper, saffron in filaments (zaʿfarān shaʿr), nadd-aloeswood, marshmallow seed, seven grains of mountain-apple, seven grains of black cumin, and seven grains of church incense. And when you have suffumigated the paper, you fold it over the name of whomever you wish, and you say: I have folded up your tongue, O So-and-so son of So-and-so [f.], away from So-and-so son of So-and-so [f.], as I have folded up this paper. Then you circle the paper about the head of the one you desire three times; and if that is not possible for you, then circle the sheet at a distance, in whatever way is contrived. Then the seeker puts it beneath his turban, between his eyes, and goes in upon whatever he desires.

This is when it is upon the name of a particular person. But if he wants it for the whole of humankind, of every female and male, then let him suffumigate it with the aforementioned incense and put it in his turban: he will see wonder upon wonder in the submission of creatures to love of him. And the condition in that is that he keep constantly to the recitation of the Throne Verse seventeen times every day; he will see wonder upon wonder. And this is its form.
Fig. 216

And among the occult properties of the noble Throne Verse for love and intimacy between two who bear hatred toward one another — and among the occult properties of that: you begin your operation in a fortunate, good hour, for what we have mentioned. Then you write the names of the two who hate one another upon a sheet and set it before you. Then you take forty grains of male frankincense, of the size /fol. 185v./ of peppercorns, and forty grains of jinn-apple. Then you divide the incense into two halves, twenty from each, and you suffumigate with two grains until the incense is completed — forty times — while you recite the Throne Verse. And every time you have recited it five times, you say: Take charge, O servant-spirits of this noble verse, of the casting of love and affection between So-and-so son of So-and-so [f.] and So-and-so son of So-and-so [f.], by the right of this sura upon you and of its blessing with you, and by the right of Him who said to the heavens and the earth: Come, willingly or unwillingly! They said: We come willingly (Q 41:11). And when you have finished your recitation, you draw the wafq whose mention comes next upon a sheet from among those sheets; and you write together with the square these noble verses and these lofty names. You say: O God, I ask You, O Living, O Self-Subsisting, O You whom eyes do not see and conjectures do not mingle with, whom describers do not describe and characterizers do not characterize; O You whose command is between the kāf and the nūn — His command, when He wills a thing, is only that He say "Be", and it is (Q 36:82): I ask You, O God, to cast love and affection between So-and-so son of So-and-so [f.] and So-and-so son of So-and-so [f.], by the right of these noble verses. They love them as God should be loved; but those who believe are stronger in love for God (Q 2:165). Had you spent all that is in the earth, you could not have joined their hearts in affection; but God joined them in affection. Truly He is Mighty, Wise (Q 8:63). And truly, in the love of good he is intense (Q 100:8). And I cast upon you a love from Me, that you might be fashioned under My eye (Q 20:39). O God, O You who created in the fourth heaven an angel half of whom is of snow and half of fire, so that the fire does not melt the snow nor the snow quench the fire, and the angel calls out with the tongue of omnipotence: All-Glorified, All-Holy, Lord of the angels and the Spirit! O God, O You who joined together snow and fire, join together the heart of Your servant So-and-so son of So-and-so [f.] and So-and-so son of So-and-so [f.]; truly You are powerful over whatever You will. [And this is] the form of the aforementioned square.
Fig. 217

And know — may God, exalted is He, grant me success in obedience to Him and in the understanding of the secrets of His names — that among the occult properties of the noble Throne Verse is [its use] for love, and for acceptance, and for standing among the great ones. So when you desire that, draw this square, which I shall set out for you, upon gazelle parchment; and the writing is with musk, saffron and rose-water; and you write around the square the Throne Verse; and you suffumigate, at the time of writing and at the time of carrying it, with Indian aloeswood, benzoin (jāwī), and ʿūd al-ṣalīb (cyclamen). So understand that. /fol. 186r./
Fig. 218

And know — may God, exalted is He, grant success to me and to you in obedience to Him and in the understanding of the secrets of His names — that I shall mention for the Throne Verse also an occult property bound up with matters of love and intimacy among the great ones, and with the casting of awe into their hearts; and it profits for meeting kings and viziers, when one carries it and recites it. And they are these verses and names. You say this blessed supplication, and it is this: O God, I ask You, O God of the first and the last, O Answerer of the invocation of those who ask — I ask You, O God, by the right of God: there is no god but He, the Living, the Self-Subsisting (Q 2:255), that You deliver me from So-and-so son of So-and-so [f.], and that You make him smitten with love for So-and-so son of So-and-so [f.]. Neither slumber nor sleep overtakes Him (Q 2:255) — even so let neither slumber nor sleep overtake So-and-so son of So-and-so [f.]; even so let him rave the whole length of his night with love of So-and-so son of So-and-so [f.]. To Him belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is in the earth (Q

2:255) — even so let the heavens and the earth be straitened upon So-and-so son of So-and-so [f.], so that he sees, in his sleep and his night, nothing but his phantom with him and the mention of him upon his tongue, from the intensity of the abiding love between them. Who is there that shall intercede with Him save by His leave?(Q 2:255) — even so let there intercede for So-and-so son of So-and-so [f.] these…

…this generous and noble verse with So-and-so son of So-and-so [f.], without the intercession of created beings, but rather by the intercession of the word of the Real. He knows what is before them and what is behind them (Q 2:255) — likewise So-and-so son of So-and-so knows that So-and-so son of So-and-so is before him and not behind his back /fol. 186v./: obedient to his command, answering his call, responding to his word, fulfilling his need, love firmly rooted in his heart. And they encompass nothing of His knowledge save what He wills. His Footstool embraces the heavens and the earth (Q 2:255) — likewise let the heart of So-and-so son of So-and-so embrace love for So-and-so son of So-and-so, as His Footstool embraces the heavens and the earth. I have widened your heart and set it beating, O So-and-so son of So-and-so, toward So-and-so son of So-and-so, as His Footstool embraces the heavens and the earth; he has no strength to be patient away from him. I have set you beating, O So-and-so son of So-and-so, toward So-and-so son of So-and-so, until you accomplish for him all his interests, and whatever he seeks and whatever he desires, without turning back and without opposition. The guarding of them does not weary Him, and He is the Exalted, the Magnificent (Q 2:255). O God, I ask You — O Allāh, O Allāh, O Allāh — that You settle love for So-and-so son of So-and-so in the heart of So-and-so son of So-and-so, so that he obeys him and disobeys no command of his, by the right of this noble verse. Take charge, O servant-spirits (khuddām) of this noble verse, of So-and-so son of So-and-so: incline his heart, and soften all his limbs with love for So-and-so son of So-and-so, by the right of this generous verse — They love them as God is loved; but those who believe are stronger in love for God (Q 2:165); Had you spent all that is in the earth, you could not have brought their hearts together; but God brought them together. Truly He is Mighty, Wise (Q 8:63); And I cast upon you love from Me (Q 20:39) — O So-and-so son of So-and-so, by the right of these noble verses.

And it is related of one of the righteous that when night fell upon him he would rise to his prayer-niche (miḥrāb) and pray as much as God willed; and when his prayer was completed he would say — this supplication is for this noble verse: "[O God,] You are You! Hope is cut off save from You, and expectations come to nothing save in You, and the ways draw their supply from none but You, O Trust of him who has no trust in any but You. I ask You, O God, by Your name, the Magnificent, the Greatest — God — there is no god but He, the Living, the Self-Subsisting (Q 2:255): You are the Living, the Abiding for ever. Neither slumber seizes Him nor sleep (Q 2:255) — for slumber and sleep belong to created beings, not to the Creator. To Him belongs whatever is in the heavens and the earth (Q 2:255): You are the God of the heavens and the earth, You are the Sustainer of the heavens and the earth, there is no god but You. Who is there that shall intercede with Him save by His leave?(Q 2:255) Who is there that has power over that over which You have power? You — all created things are [subject to] the subduing might of Your magnificence. O You who knows what is before them and what is behind them, and they encompass nothing of His knowledge save what He wills. His Footstool embraces the heavens and the earth (Q 2:255): You are He who has embraced all things in mercy and knowledge, and You are Knower of all things. The guarding of them does not weary Him, and He is the Exalted, the Magnificent (Q 2:255). Our Lord, our Lord! Our Master, our Master! Our Patron, our Patron! You are He who gives and withholds, and You are He who raises and lowers; and You are He who sees and hears, and nothing in the earth or in the heaven is hidden from You. I ask You by the hiddenness of Your gentleness and by the majesty of Your might that You bless and grant peace to our master Muḥammad, the greatest beloved, the honoured Prophet, the magnified Messenger, our master and our prophet Muḥammad — God bless him and grant him peace; and I ask You by the standing of the people of his House, the good and the pure, by the standing of his companions all together, and by the standing of the Successors and of those who follow the Successors in excellence until the Day of Judgement: I ask You to gather me in their throng and beneath their banners, and to supply me with their supply. Amen, O Lord of the worlds!" Whoever communes with God with this /fol. 187r./ blessed supplication in the depth of the night and asks God, exalted is He, He gives him all that he has sought; and God is the possessor of magnificent bounty. So understand and ponder.

And among the occult properties of the noble Throne Verse: if one of you has a need among the needs of this world and of the world to come, let him rise in the depth of the night and pray four rakʿas, reciting in each rakʿa the Fātiḥa once and the Throne Verse ten times; and let him raise his head and his hands to heaven and invoke with this supplication: "O God, I ask You — O Allāh, O Allāh, O Allāh, O al-Ḥayy (the Living), O al-Qayyūm (the Self-Subsisting), O You whom neither slumber seizes nor sleep — I ask You, O God, by the sanctity of the Throne Verse with You, that You do for me such-and-such, and that You grant me all my desires and my purposes and what I seek from You" — and you ask for your need and name it; for it is a right upon God, exalted is He, that He accomplish it. Then pray for the Prophet — God bless him and grant him peace — at the beginning of your undertaking and at the end of it, and your operation will prosper, if God, exalted is He, wills. And God is the Granter of success.

And among the occult properties of the noble Throne Verse: whoever recites it by day, God — exalted is He — guards him on that day; and if he recites it by night, God — exalted is He — guards him during his night. And whoever recites the Throne Verse after every prayer, all his sins are forgiven him. And among the occult properties of the Throne

Verse: whoever recites it after every prayer, God forgives him his sins and effaces from him his evil deeds until the next prayer. And among the occult properties of the Throne Verse: whoever recites it at his sleeping, it is a protective charm for him against the accursed Satan. And among the occult properties of the Throne Verse: [whoever recites it] when he is angry, and spits to his left, the Satan slinks back — his own satan — and there departs from him his anger, by the leave of God, exalted is He.

Let us now set down this blessed supplication for the noble Throne Verse. I have abridged the exposition of it and the discourse upon it, lest it fall into the hands of one who does not know it, and he invoke with it and be answered. It is a mighty supplication, majestic in worth, magnificent in proof, magnificent in worth. You say: God — there is no god but He (Q 2:255) — He is alone in abiding and in permanence. The essence of created beings: their reality does not subsist alongside His essence, nor their attributes alongside His attributes, nor their names alongside His names, nor their acts alongside His acts; and there is none other than Him, not one. There is no beauty save His beauty in reality, and no majesty save His majesty, and no perfection save His perfection; and He is everlasting, ever returning in His perfection, the Living, the Self-Subsisting, abiding upon His Throne by the perpetuity of His kingship. And all creatures are led to the knowledge of Him, and they know that He is One in His kingship, Unique in His everlastingness, mighty in His eternity. Despite the diversity of their intellects and of their religions, they all /fol. 187v./ return to the reality of knowledge, and they know that He is the Creator, the Provider, the Giver of life and the Bringer of death, and that the whole affair returns to Him. As for the gnostics and the verifiers (muḥaqqiqūn): they have wandered lost in the reality of the knowledge of that which has illumined their hearts and their sights through the disclosure of the realities of the knowledge of His handiworks. They have wandered lost in the seas of His love and of what He has bestowed upon them, and they have plunged into the waves of the fathomless deeps of the seas — and there is no buffeting against His power. They confessed their incapacity to attain the knowledge of Him, and they drowned in the seas of His dominion; and they knew and verified that there is no god but He; and it pointed to His being Living and Self-Subsisting. So He gave life to their hearts and illumined their inner sights and their inmost hearts, so that they beheld in existence none but Him, and no Lord but Him alone, and they confessed their incapacity before Him. [Neither] slumber seizes Him nor sleep (Q 2:255) — that is: no lassitude seizes Him away from the creating of things made, and no sleep away from the apprehending of things known. Truly His command, when He wills a thing — and He says: Be! and it is (Q 36:82). So glory be to Him in whose hand is the dominion of all things, and unto Him you shall be returned (Q 36:83). All existent things hallow Him above indwelling and above likeness, above union, above beginning and end, above conjunction and separation: the like of whom there is nothing (Q 42:11). He is before things; and the return of creatures and their submission is unto Him. The First and the Term, One, Unique, alone in Himself in the hidden things, beyond eyes and understandings. To Him belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is in the earth (Q 2:255). And all beings bear witness to Him and are knowers of His handiworks, [testifying] that He is the God of the earths and the heavens. Who is there that shall intercede with Him save by His leave?(Q 2:255) There glorify Him the people of the heavens and of the earths: and there is nothing that does not glorify Him with praise, but you do not understand their glorification (Q 17:44). Every speaker, then, [speaks] by His leave, and every utterer, then, by His knowledge. He is knower of all things and independent of all things; and everything is in need of Him, submissive to Him, abased before Him. He knows what is before them and what is behind them, and they encompass nothing of His knowledge (Q 2:255). Glory be to You! We have no knowledge save what You have taught us; truly You are the All-Knowing, the Wise (Q 2:32). He knows what is in the land and the sea; not a leaf falls but He knows it, nor is there a grain in the darknesses of the earth, nor anything moist or dry, but it is in a clear Book (Q 6:59). And they encompass nothing of His knowledge save what He wills (Q 2:255). He has encompassed all things in knowledge (Q 65:12). And God is encompassing them from behind; nay, it is a majestic Qurʾān, upon a preserved Tablet (Q 85:20–22). And His power has encompassed the dominion of His might, so that all things journey unto Him. Our Lord, You have embraced all things in mercy and knowledge (Q 40:7). The spirits departed, and the faces were disfigured and wandered lost within the temples of their phantoms, and disposed themselves among the fashioned works of their traces, and took shape within the moulds of the spiritual beings, for the witnessing of the diversity of the forms within the moulds of composition, in the circuit of the barzakhs, for the manifestation of the decree upon the indication and the manifestation of knowledge. Their outward is the outward of power, and their inward is the inward of the Command and the secret of the [divine] confirming, for the reception of the courses of the decree and of free disposal by it. His Footstool embraces /fol. 188r./ the heavens and the earth, and the guarding of them does not weary Him, and He is the Exalted, the Magnificent (Q 2:255). Widen for us, out of Your self-subsistence, a knowledge and an understanding whereby we may dispose within the beings — there is no power and no strength save in You. I have raised up my need to You and my destitution before You: so do not disappoint my hope of You, for You are the All-Embracing, the Generous, the Magnificent Lord. I ask You by the wellspring of the life of the spiritual souls, and by the lights of the secrets of Your name, the Magnificent, the Greatest, by whose self-disclosure was cleft open the thirst of the innermost hearts of the people of a love whose proof is manifest — so that they wandered lost in the valleys of the purity of their inmost secrets and the lights of their essences, and cried out: O You whose Footstool embraces the heavens and the earth, and the guarding of them does not weary Him, and He is the Exalted, the Magnificent (Q 2:255)! I ask You, O al-Wāsiʿ (the All-

Embracing), O al-ʿAlīm (the All-Knowing), O al-ʿAlī (the High), O al-ʿAẓīm (the Magnificent), O al-Karīm (the Generous), O al-Raḥīm (the Compassionate), O al-Raʾūf (the Ever-Gentle), O al-Ḥalīm (the Forbearing), O You who are God — there is no god but He, the Living…

…the Self-Subsisting. Neither slumber seizes Him nor sleep. To Him belongs whatever is in the heavens and the earth. The guarding of them does not weary Him, and He is the Exalted, the Magnificent (Q 2:255). I ask You, O God, by the right of these mighty verses and generous names, that You illumine our hearts, and widen our provision, and refine our characters. O Comforter of hearts, O Veiler of faults, O Dispeller of distresses, O Forgiver of sins, O Knower of all unseen things! You have known what has been of my asking and of my excusing myself in my retreat (khalwa), and of my seeking pardon for my slip and my disavowal of my sin. And You, O God, are best acquainted with my aspiration, and aware of my intention, and knowing of my inner disposition; the Master of all Dominion, my Lord, who holds my forelock, my goal in my request, my hope in my hardship, my comforter in my solitude, the merciful toward my tears, He who grants me release from my stumbling, the Answerer of my invocation. And if I have fallen short of what You commanded me and have committed what You forbade me, yet by Your standing You have protected me and by Your veiling You have veiled me. So, O most generous of the generous, O goal of the seekers, O Master of the Day of Judgement: You know what is hidden in the conscience, and You are the Disposer of the affairs of small and great. If You have accomplished my need, it is by Your bounty. I ask You to make me an intercessor for my own soul, and to have mercy upon me by Your mercy, O Most Merciful of the merciful. I ask You, O God, by the right of this generous verse and of the names of understanding (al-asmāʾ al-fahmiyya), that You bless and grant peace to our master Muḥammad and to the family of Muḥammad, and that You give me my request and what I have sought from You. O Allāh, O Allāh, O Allāh, O Lord of the worlds!

And among the occult properties of the noble Throne Verse: if the servant is much given to sins and offences, and desires repentance for what he has perpetrated and separation from what he has done, let him rise in the White Nights of whatever month it may be — that is, the thirteenth /fol. 188v./, the fourteenth and the fifteenth. Let him purify his garments and his place, and let him rise in the depth of the night, and perform the ablution, and pray four rakʿas, reciting in the first rakʿa the Fātiḥa once and the Throne Verse seven times; and he does in every rakʿa the like of that first one. And when he has given the salām, let him sit and ask forgiveness of God, exalted is He, the Magnificent, seventy times, and pray for the Prophet — God bless him and grant him peace — seventy times. And the form of the prayer upon the Prophet — God bless him and grant him peace — is that you say: "O God, bless our master Muḥammad with a blessing whereby You deliver us from all terrors and afflictions, and whereby You accomplish for us all needs, and whereby You purify us of all ambiguities, and whereby You raise us to the highest degrees, and whereby You bring us to the furthest ends of good things in life and in death — a blessing that You store up for the Day of the

Greatest Terror and its dread; and upon his family, and his kin, and his companions, and grant peace." Then you begin by reciting this blessed supplication. You say: "O God, You are the Ever-Relenting toward whoever repents, and He who draws near whoever turns [to Him], and the Remover of the darkness of the veil. You know the treachery of the eyes and what the breasts conceal; and You have power over all things; and unto You the affairs return; and by You are evils repelled. O God, I ask You by the secret of Your name for a secret from Your secret, and a light from Your light, and a spirit from Your Command, that shall bequeath to me stillness before what You have decreed; and grant me a success from You that shall awaken what is heedless in me, and teach what is ignorant in me, and make plain my road to You, and be my companion in the going out and the returning. For in You is my striving, and upon You is my reliance, and unto You is my return, and before You is my falling. You know the reality of my affair and of my asking; with You are my secret and my open state. You are exalted above the marks of originated things, and transcendent above defects and afflictions, and Your knowledge is [too high] to be contested by ambiguities. I ask You, O God, for a repentance whereby You efface my slips, and whereby You make my work weigh heavy, and whereby You set right my outward, and whereby You purify my inward, and whereby You gather my scattered state, and whereby You hallow my innermost secret, and whereby You make my sanctification easy, and whereby You purify my soul, and whereby You cleanse me of my defilement. And grant me a light from You whereby I may walk among men; truly You are the Bestower, the Giver of lights, the Discloser of secrets, and everything with You is by measure. O al-Ḥayy (the Living), O al-Qayyūm (the Self-Subsisting), O Dhū l-Jalāl wa-l-Ikrām (Possessor of Majesty and Honour)!" And God bless our master Muḥammad and his family and his companions, and grant them abundant peace.

And among the occult properties of the noble Throne Verse: whoever fears the outcome of some affair and wishes to know it and to come out of it — let him purify himself and put on pure, clean garments, and purify the place in which he sits in seclusion. Then, when he has prayed the last night prayer (ʿishāʾ) /fol. 189r./, let him pray two rakʿas before the witr prayer, reciting in each rakʿa the Fātiḥa once and the Throne Verse eleven times. And when he has given the salām, let him recite the Throne Verse twenty-one times, and recite the sura Truly We sent it down on the Night of Power (Q 97:1) once, and Sūrat al-Ikhlāṣthree times, and the two suras of refuge-seeking (al-muʿawwidhatān) once. And let him say: "O God, I have sought an omen by Your ancient speech, so show me that which is hidden away. O God, show me in this night of mine all that I have asked about and what I have not asked about, and make plain to me the way out of this affair which I fear and am wary of. O God, if it be good for me, show me whiteness and greenness; and if it be evil for me and against me, show me blackness and redness. And [I ask] that You send me a servant-spirit (khādim) from among the servant-spirits of this noble verse, the Throne Verse, who shall tell me in my sleep what is kept hidden from me. My God, You are the Real: make plain to me the truth, O Real — the Real! Truly You have power over all things." Then you name what you want and what you seek. Then you pray the witr prayer, and you lie down upon your right side, and you pray for our master Muḥammad — God bless him and grant him peace — to the measure of your capacity, and you sleep, and you set your mind upon your need. For God, blessed and exalted is He, sends you a servant-spirit from among the servant-spirits of this verse, and he informs you of all that you want and all that you seek, and makes clear to you your need, and what is good for you and what is evil against you. And if you do not see in your night what you seek and what you have asked about, then repeat the operation and the prayer on the second night and on the third, and you will see what you seek. So make your intention sincere, for the intention precedes the act; and God guides whom He wills to a straight path. And know the worth of what has reached you, for it makes you independent of much learning.

And among the occult properties of the noble Throne Verse: whoever is harmed by passionate love and infatuation and distracted longing toward some person, and fears scandal from people or from his own household — he recites the Throne Verse five times over a glass cup with musk and saffron and rose-water; then he sets it out beneath the open sky, after he has written the name of the person whose love he wishes to be rid of. Then, when morning comes, he dissolves the writing with rose-water and drinks it on an empty stomach. He does that […] times over three days; and God, exalted is He, will make him forget that person and will pluck the love of him out of his heart. And the intention precedes the act: whoever makes his intention sincere attains his wish.

And know — may God grant you and me success in obedience to Him and in the understanding of His secrets — that the Throne Verse has many occult properties and majestic, abundant benefits. It benefits one who is afraid, when trembling comes upon him: that departs from him by the leave of God, exalted is He. And among its occult properties: it is written for pain of the heart, and palpitation, and pain of the liver, and griping of the bowels. It is written as we have mentioned /fol. 189v./ in a pure vessel three times, and the one afflicted drinks it, saying as he drinks it: "I have intended healing from such-and-such an ailment" — and he names the ailment. For God, exalted is He, by the blessing of the noble verse, heals him and restores him — by the blessing of the noble verse, by the leave of God, exalted is He; and God is the Healer and the Restorer. And among the occult properties of the Throne Verse: it is of benefit for the dispelling of [the disease of] the spleen and of its pain. Let the noble verse be written and hung above the spleen, and God will heal him and restore him, by the blessing of the noble names.

And among the occult properties of the Throne Verse, for headache and migraine: let the Throne Verse be written upon gazelle parchment, if that be possible, or upon clean paper (kāghid); and there is written with it His words, exalted is He: Had We sent down this Qurʾān upon a mountain, you would have seen it humbled, split asunder out of the fear of God. And these similitudes We strike for men, that they may reflect (Q 59:21) — to the end of the sura; and His words, exalted is He: And to Him belongs whatsoever dwells in the night and the day; and He is the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing (Q 6:13). Be still, O pain, and headache, and migraine, and throbbing, away from the bearer of this writing of mine, as the Throne of the All-Merciful is still! And by the secret of these noble, blessed, lofty letters —

— still the distress of him over whom I have pronounced these names, by the right of these names! God is the Healer, God is the Sufficer, God is the Restorer. So God will suffice you against them, and He is the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing (Q 2:137). And there is no power and no strength save in God, the High, the Mighty. This is among what has been tried and proved sound.
Know, O my brother — may God grant you and me success in obedience to Him and in the unveiling of the secrets of His names — that this noble verse, I mean the Throne Verse, has occult properties…

…beyond counting and beyond number, for it is the greatest verse in the Book of God, exalted is He. And among the greatest of its occult properties is what I now mention to you, namely this: I was sitting before my master Abū ʿAbd Allāh al-Andalusī, and we were conferring together upon some of the sciences, when there came in upon us a man trembling like a palm-frond in a raging wind. Then he gave the greeting, and fell upon the shaykh's hand, kissing it and weeping. So the shaykh said to him: What ails you, O man, and what has made you weep? The man said: My lord, I am in fear of certain enemies, that one of them should treacherously assail me with harm; and I have no power against him. And I have come to you, my lord, in the hope that you may relieve me of my care and remove from me my distress. And when the shaykh heard this speech from the man, he said to him: Rejoice, O man, and fear not — if God, exalted is He, wills — after this day, from anyone. Then the shaykh took a slip of paper (ruqʿa) and wrote upon it: "I take refuge with God from the accursed Satan. In the name of God, the All-Merciful, the Compassionate. And God bless our master Muḥammad and his family and his companions, and grant abundant peace." Then he wrote the Fātiḥa of the Book, and His words, exalted is He, /fol. 190r./ the Throne Verse; then you write Sūrat al-Ikhlāṣand the two suras of refuge-seeking (al-Muʿawwidhatān); then you write His words, exalted is He: And fear not; truly you are among the secure (Q 28:31); You shall fear neither being overtaken, nor shall you dread (Q 20:77); And fear not, you two; truly I am with you both, hearing and seeing (Q 20:46); Fear not; you have escaped from the wrongdoing folk (Q 28:25); Two men of those who feared, upon whom God had bestowed favour, said: Enter upon them by the gate; for when you have entered it, you shall be the victors. And upon God rely, if you are believers (Q 5:23); Fear not; truly you, you are the higher (Q 20:68). O God, guard me with Your eye that does not sleep, and shelter me within Your shelter that cannot be assailed, and forgive me by Your power over me, that I may not perish; for You are my hope. My Lord, how many a favour have You bestowed upon me for which my thanksgiving to You was little, and yet You did not deprive me! And O You who have seen me amid trials and did not disgrace me! O Possessor of kindness that is never cut off, and O Possessor of blessings that are never numbered: I ask You, O God, that You bless our master Muḥammad and the family of our master Muḥammad, and that You preserve me and guard me from my enemies and from whoever intends me evil or harm. And turn back, O God, his violence upon him, and set his good between his eyes and his evil beneath his feet. And whoever desires for me evil, or treachery, or guile — let it return upon him, and make it cleave fast to him. And God turned back those who disbelieved in their rage; they attained no good. And God sufficed the believers in the fighting; and God is Strong, Mighty (Q 33:25). Deaf, dumb, blind — so they do not see; so they do not speak; so they do not talk. A day on which they shall not speak, nor shall they be given leave to make excuses (Q 77:35–36). Ṣād (Q 38:1). Qāf (Q 50:1). Nūn (Q 68:1). So God will suffice you against them, and He is the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing (Q 2:137). And there is no power and no strength save in God, the High, the Mighty. Then the shaykh folded the slip and handed it to the man, and said to him: Put it in your turban, for you will be safe from every harm. And the man never saw any evil come upon him thereafter.

And know, my brother, that these names of mighty worth — none has carried them but that God, exalted is He, delivered him from what he fears and guards against. And if he goes in with them upon a tyrannical ruler, he is safe from his evil; and none disputes with their bearer but that he overcomes him and subdues him, by their blessing. And their excellences are renowned among the learned and among those who know their worth. And God supports with His help whom He wills (Q 3:13). And God is the Possessor of mighty bounty (Q 3:74).

A blessed benefit, for guarding against enemies and against the fear of highwaymen and others. One of the righteous — may God, blessed and exalted, have mercy upon him — said: We halted, on one of our journeys, by a flowing river; and a people came to us and said: no one has halted in this place but that his baggage has been plundered. So my companions departed out of fear, and I stayed behind, on account of a noble hadith I had heard from Ibn ʿUmar — may God, exalted is He, be pleased with them both — from the Prophet, God bless him and grant him peace, that he said: ((Whoever recites thirty-three /fol. 190v./ verses from the Book of God, exalted is He, no ravening beast of prey and no marauding thief shall harm him that night, and he shall be granted well-being in himself, his family, and his property, until morning.)) So when evening came, I did not sleep until I saw a company who had come brandishing their swords to draw near to me; but they could not reach me. And when I rose in the morning I departed, and there met me a shaykh upon a horse who said to me: O you, are you a human or a jinnī? I said: A human, of the children of Adam. He said to me: What is your case? We came upon you this night more than seventy times, and every time there was interposed between us and you a wall of iron. I said to him: Ibn ʿUmar — may God be pleased with him — related to me, from the Messenger of God, God bless him and grant him peace, that he said: ((Whoever recites thirty-three verses from the Book of God, exalted is He, in a night, no ravening beast of prey and no marauding thief shall harm him, and he shall be in the safekeeping of God, exalted is He, until morning.)) And when the shaykh heard that, he dismounted from his horse and kissed my head, and gave God, exalted is He, a covenant that he would never return to what he had been doing. And these verses that have been mentioned are recited [as follows]: four verses from the beginning of Sūrat al-Baqara, up to His words, exalted is He, the successful (Q 2:5); and the noble Throne Verse and the two verses after it, up to His words abiding therein (Q 2:257); and the three last verses of al-Baqara, To God belongs whatever is in the heavens and the earth; and whether you disclose what is in yourselves or conceal it (Q 2:284), to the end of the sura; and three verses from al-Aʿrāf, His words, exalted is He, Indeed your Lord is God, who created the heavens and the earth in six days (Q 7:54), up to His words, exalted is He, of those who do good (Q 7:56); and ten verses from the beginning of al-Ṣāffāt, up to His words, exalted is He, clinging (Q 37:11); and the end of al-Isrāʾ, Say: Call upon God, or call upon the All-Merciful; whichever you call upon (Q 17:110), to the end of the sura; and two verses from Sūrat al-Raḥmān, O company of jinn and mankind, if you are able to pass beyond the confines of the heavens and the earth, then pass beyond! You shall not pass beyond save by an authority (Q 55:33), up to His words, exalted is He, you will not be helped (Q 55:35); and the closing verses of al-Ḥashr, His words, exalted is He, Had We sent down this Qurʾān upon a mountain, you would have seen it humbled, split asunder out of the fear of God; and these similitudes We strike for mankind, that they may reflect (Q 59:21), to the end of the sura; and two verses from Sūrat Say: it has been revealed to me (Q 72:1), up to His words, exalted is He, And the places of worship belong to God (Q 72:18); And He — exalted be the majesty of our Lord — has taken neither consort nor child (Q 72:3), up to His words, exalted is He, outrageous falsehood (Q 72:4).

And know that these verses are called the Verses of Guarding (āyāt al-ḥaras); and it is said that in them is a healing for a hundred maladies, such as leprosy (judhām), vitiligo (baraṣ), and the like. And it is related from Muḥammad b. ʿAlī — may God, exalted is He, be pleased with them both — [who said]: I recited them over a shaykh who had been struck with hemiplegia (al-fālij), and God, exalted is He, took that away from him, by the leave of God, exalted is He, and by the blessing of His eternal speech. So understand that, and you will be rightly guided. And whoever engraves this noble wafq /fol. 191r./ upon a signet-ring of silver, or upon a plate of the same, in the first hour of the day of Friday — which is from sunrise until the shadow measures twenty-eight feet — then whoever does that sees marvels in himself. And it is for love, for acceptance, for awe, and for the widening of provision. And this is its form:

Wherever you may be, God will bring you all together; indeed God is powerful over everything (Q 2:148)

A majestic benefit, for the meeting of kings, rulers, viziers, judges, and governors, and of the masters of the pen and the holders of office. It is set down in the exaltation of the Sun, or in the exaltation of Jupiter, upon a plate of gold, or of silver, or of red copper; and let the engraver be fasting. And it is suffumigated, at the time of its engraving and at the time of its being carried and of the need for it, with Indian aloeswood, benzoin (jāwī), mastic, nadd aloeswood, and saffron. So understand that, and you will be rightly guided, if God, exalted is He, wills. And this is the form of its arrangement, as you see. So understand that, and you will be rightly guided, if God, exalted is He, wills. /fol. 191v./

And it is related of one of the righteous that he said: I had a need [to lay] before God, exalted is He, and I remained thirty years asking God, exalted is He, for it; and with all that I did not despair of it. Then one night I took to my bed and slept, and behold, one was saying: Take these adjurations that are beneath your head, and adjure [God] by them in your need, and it shall be granted. So I awoke, and I found these adjurations written upon a scroll in separated letters. So I gathered them together, and behold, they were as you see. And I have never adjured [God] by them in any need but that it was granted, by the leave of God, exalted is He. And they are these verses:

By the humility of hearts at the prostration, to You, O my Master, without any denial; and by You, O God, O Friend — for nothing draws near to You in the solemnity of covenants; and by Your Footstool, crowned with light, [rising] to Your mighty, glorious Throne; and by what was beneath Your Throne in truth, before the creation of heaven and the sound of the thunders —
that was when You had never at any time ceased to be a God known by divine oneness (tawḥīd).

And you say, when you have finished these noble verses: I ask You, O God, that You bless and grant peace to our master Muḥammad and to the family of our master Muḥammad, and that You accomplish my need, which is such-and-such. For God, exalted is He, will accomplish it, if God, exalted is He, wills.

And there follows it this blessed supplication, which is the supplication of the noble Throne Verse. /fol. 192r./ You say: O Living, O Self-Subsisting! You are God, other than whom there is no god; truly I was among the wrongdoers. I ask You by Your self-subsistence (qayyūmiyya) that You establish me through You unto You; and I ask You by Your life for a life for my heart, and for well-being in that, in religion and in this world and in the hereafter and in what lies between the two. And preserve all of that for me, O You whom the guarding of nothing wearies! O High, O Magnificent — until I meet You while You are pleased with me: O God, in the best of states from You, and in the most easeful of minds, without trial and without punishment, neither in religion, nor in this world, nor in the hereafter — by Your mercy, O Most Merciful of the merciful.
And know, my brother — may God grant you and me success in obedience to Him, and illumine our hearts with the light of gnosis of Him — I used often to persevere in the recitation of the Throne Verse…

…and the closing verses of Sūrat al-Baqara, from His words, exalted is He, The Messenger has believed (Q 2:285), to the end of the sura; then the opening [verses] of Āl ʿImrān, up to His words, exalted is He, the Mighty, the Wise (Q 3:6), together with the two verses, His words, exalted is He, Say: O God, Master of the kingdom— up to His words, exalted is He — without reckoning (Q 3:26–27). Then you say: O God, I ask You for soundness of fear, and the overmastering of yearning, and the coming of knowledge, and the perpetuity of reflection. I ask You, O

God, for the secret of secrets that wards off harms, so that we may have no abiding-place along with sin and blemish. And give us life, and guide us to act by these words which You spread out for us upon the tongue of Your Messenger, and with which You tried Abraham Your friend: and he fulfilled them. He said: I am making you a leader for mankind. He said: And of my progeny? He said: My covenant does not reach the wrongdoers (Q 2:124). So make us of those who do good, of his progeny and of the progeny of Adam and Noah; and lead us along the paths of the imams of the God-fearing. O God, I have wronged myself with much wronging, and none forgives sins but You; so forgive me and have mercy upon me. There is no god but You. Glory be to You! Truly I was among the wrongdoers (Q 21:87). O God, O High, O Magnificent, O Forbearing, O All-Knowing, O All-Hearing, O All-Seeing, O Willing, O Powerful, O Self-Subsisting, O All-Merciful, O Compassionate, O You who are Yāh Yāh, O First, O Last, O Manifest, O Hidden! Blessed is Your name, Possessor of Majesty and Honour. And relent toward me. And enter my names beneath Your names, and my attributes beneath Your attributes, and my acts beneath Your acts, unto the degree of safety and the casting off of regret. And send down a secret with which sins do no harm at all, and make for me from it a face whereby needs are accomplished — for the heart, and the intellect, and the spirit, and the yearning, and the soul, and the body. O God, join me to Your mighty name, together with whose name nothing in the earth nor in the heaven can do harm — and He is the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing. And grant me from Yourself nobility (karāma) and the manifestation of leadership (imāma); and be for me, in that wherewith I have been tried, [as You are] for the imams of guidance among Your learned ones. ḤifẓĀyetleri (the Protective Verses)
Manbaʿ Uṣūl al-Ḥikma, vol. II, p. 121

These Protective Verses should be written out toward dawn, on the night of the first Friday of an Arabic lunar month. First perform a clean ritual ablution (abdest) and, seeking Allah's pleasure, pray two rak'ahs of the Prayer of Need (ḥāja namazi). Then, using musk and saffron, write these Protective Verses on a clean sheet of paper. Nothing can harm whoever carries this written amulet (ḥirz) upon his person. By Allah Almighty's leave, that person is kept safe and protected from every kind of evil, from grief, from sorrow, and from anxiety and distress.

If these Protective Verses are written on a piece of paper and placed on or inside a piece of property, that property will not be lost or ruined. If placed inside a building, by Allah Almighty's leave that building is protected from collapse and from fire.

If these Protective Verses are written on a piece of paper, magic will have no effect on whoever carries this written amulet upon his person. And if magic has already been worked upon him, it is nullified.

If a person writes these Protective Verses on a piece of paper, carries this written amulet upon himself, and takes them up daily as a wird (a regular devotional recitation), reading them every day, then by Allah Almighty's leave he is kept safe from every [II 122] kind of evil and calamity. Magic will not even affect him. He is protected from the harm of jinn and of men.

The Five Noble Verses with Ten Qāfs Each
Manbaʿ Uṣūl al-Ḥikma, vol. II, p. 124

The Prophet Muḥammad (peace and blessings be upon him) said: "Recite these Five Noble Verses at all times." Shaykh Abdulwahid (may Allah sanctify his secret) says: Each of these five verses contains ten (10) letters qāf. In the science of letters, the numerical value (abjad — the system that assigns a number to every letter of the alphabet) of the letter qāf is one hundred (100), so the total comes to five thousand (5000). Allah Almighty gave these five verses to the community of Muḥammad and to the Kutub (the Pole, the axis-saint of the age). Judgement in the warding-off of calamities is passed by means of these five verses. Whoever recites these five verses with sincerity (Ikhlāṣ) will not be deprived of the special graces granted to the Kutub. I myself attained the rank of Kutub through these five verses. During the pilgrimage season I met with Khidr (peace be upon him), who advised me to recite these five verses. Because I recited these five verses, I found my [spiritual] stations through the secret power of these verses.

[II 125] Shaykh Yahya Shirwani (may Allah sanctify his secret) says: Through these five verses I reached the rank of Kutbu'l-aktāb (the Pole of Poles, the highest of the axis-saints). Those I met would both recite them and carry them written upon their persons. I saw this and asked, "Why do you recite this? What is its property?" They said: "If a person recites these five verses, his enemies and indeed all people become subjugated (musahhar) to him. His enemies can do him no harm." Shaykh Ma'ruf al-Karkhi (may Allah sanctify his secret) says: I met with the Kutub. They would recite these five noble verses every day and carry them upon their persons, and thereby prevailed over their enemies. Whoever harboured evil intent toward them would have all manner of calamities fall upon his own head.
Ibrahim ibn Adham (may Allah sanctify his secret) says: Whoever recites these five verses and carries them written upon himself will find his enemies' tongues bound.
Shaykh Bayezid-i Bistami (may Allah sanctify his secret) says: I recited these five noble verses for seven days and attained the rank of Kutbu'l-aktāb. The Kutub revealed his secret to me.

Shaykh Kirmani (may Allah sanctify his secret) said: In this world there are four thousand (4000) persons empowered to exercise spiritual authority (taṣarruf) — drawn from the Rijalu'l-gayb (the Hidden Men, the unseen order of saints), the Budelā (the Substitutes), the Ewtād (the Pegs), and the Kutub (the Pole). All of them exercise their authority by means of these five verses. Whoever continues to recite them, and writes them out and carries them properly upon himself, becomes a master of spiritual authority both outwardly and inwardly. He exercises his authority in both the higher and the lower worlds, and moreover comes to meet both the Kutub and the Rijalu'l-gayb.

According to a report transmitted from Ibn Mas'ud (may Allah be pleased with him): the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him) used to recite these five verses both at home and while travelling, and in battle, and thereby gained the upper hand over the unbelievers and the hypocrites. Allah Almighty would aid him and grant him the means to achieve his conquests.

According to a report transmitted from Aisha al-Siddiqa (may Allah be pleased with her), the Pride of Creation (peace and blessings be upon him) said: Whoever writes out these five verses — in which there are fifty qāfs — on a Friday, washes off what he has written with water, and drinks that water, will have placed within himself a thousand cures, established a thousand states of health, set down a thousand mercies, a thousand measures of compassion, a thousand certainties, a thousand strengths, and sent down a hundred thousand lights. Every kind of illness will be drawn out and taken from him, and his sorrow and grief will be lifted.

Shaykh Muhyiddin Ibn al-'Arabi (may Allah sanctify his secret) says: The Noble Qur'an has 6,666 verses. I saw a commentary (tefsir) on the Word of Allah in Egypt; it ran to 660 volumes. In that commentary it was recorded thus: within the Noble Qur'an there are five verses. If a person recites these five verses once a day, or once a week, or even once a month, Allah Almighty grants that person rank both in this world and in the hereafter, and in Paradise He raises him degree upon degree.

[II 126] To overwhelm one's enemies and to repel the envious, if these five noble verses are recited three times, or even just once, in the morning and in the evening, these verses themselves become the very elixir that brings about the effect.

The Two Noble Verses That Contain All Twenty-nine Letters
Manbaʿ Uṣūl al-Ḥikma, vol. II, p. 131
Imam Yāfiī, may his secret be sanctified, has said: in the Noble Qur'an there are two noble verses in which all twenty-nine letters of the alphabet are found.

These two verses are written on a plate; the writing is then dissolved with rose oil or olive oil, and the plate is set over a fire. While the oil is boiling, the Fātiḥa (the Qur'an's opening surah) is recited twenty-nine times and breathed over the plate. If the whole body of the sick person is then anointed with this oil, every affliction on the body — boils, rheumatism, sorcery, bewitchment, and swelling — vanishes that same day, and health [II 132] is restored. These two noble verses also have a great effect against such outward afflictions as fear, shuddering, agitation, sorrow, and grief.
